name: Commenter AI
tagline: AI sales conversation prioritization across LinkedIn, Gmail, and Google Calendar — so revenue threads stop getting buried.
description:
Commenter AI helps founders, AEs, and recruiters who run many active deals across LinkedIn, email, and meetings. Instead of scanning every inbox, users label revenue conversations once and get a prioritized daily view of which threads need attention — ranked by context, timing, next steps, sentiment, and calendar signals.

AI drafting is part of the product, but the core job is prioritization and deal awareness: keep revenue threads separate from noise, show who owes the next move, and draft replies when speed matters without auto-sending.

coverImage.alt: Commenter AI — prioritized sales conversations across LinkedIn, Gmail, and Calendar

problem: Sellers managing 10+ active deals jump between LinkedIn, Gmail, and Google Calendar. The loudest thread wins attention, quiet buyers slip, and half-won deals stall because nobody has a single ordered view of what needs action today.
approach: Build a lightweight conversation layer on top of the channels sellers already use. Connect LinkedIn, Gmail, and Calendar; let users mark revenue threads; then rank those threads by deal context instead of forcing a full CRM workflow.
solution: A prioritization product that surfaces revenue conversations in a clear daily order, with thread context, ownership of the next step, sentiment and meeting signals, and AI-assisted drafting for comments and DMs when the user chooses to reply faster.
features: LinkedIn + Gmail + Google Calendar connected in one prioritized view
Revenue conversation labeling to separate deals from inbox noise
Ranking by context, timing, next steps, sentiment, and meeting signals
Clear ownership of who owes the next move
AI drafting for LinkedIn comments and DMs without auto-send
Daily focus list for sellers running many parallel deals
architecture: Integration-heavy AI product: OAuth-connected messaging and calendar sources feed a ranking and context layer. The UI presents prioritized conversations and drafting helpers; the system does not replace a full CRM or auto-blast outreach.
